display.description:
Up to 5 affected applications at the end of the selected period, with the number of unavailable replicas beside each name. For example, 1 means one configured instance is not available. Check scheduling, image pulls and readiness probes. A short gap during an update can be normal.

Measurement details:
Only workloads with fewer available copies than configured are listed. The value is the number missing, not a count of failures. Deployment, StatefulSet and DaemonSet names identify the owner. A brief rollout can create a temporary gap. No matching source data stays empty.
display.name: Which applications have unavailable replicas?

display.description:
Bytes queued by collectors for delivery to SUSE Observability. A growing queue can indicate a network, authentication or backend issue.

Measurement details:
Bytes buffered by collectors before delivery to SUSE Observability. Zero is healthy: no backlog is waiting to be sent. A growing or persistent queue suggests network, authentication or receiver trouble. An absent series is not zero.

Bytes buffered by collectors before delivery to SUSE Observability. Zero is healthy: no backlog is waiting to be sent. A growing or persistent queue suggests network, authentication or receiver trouble. An absent series is not zero.

Small temporary peaks are normal. Persistent growth suggests a receiver or connection problem. If sending stops completely, this series also stops arriving.
display.name: Metrics waiting to be delivered

display.description:
Estimated retry attempts by collectors. Inspect collector logs and delivery queues when retries persist.

Measurement details:
Zero is expected in a stable period. Logs distinguish DNS, certificates, authentication, and HTTP 503 receiver failures.
display.name: Metric delivery retries in 15 minutes

display.description:
Percentage of known servers with successful operating-system collection. Missing visibility is different from an unavailable server.

Measurement details:
Healthy OS collectors divided by known nodes. Below 100% means at least one server is missing visibility.
display.name: Servers with working OS metrics

display.description:
Highest measured server CPU-use percentage. Colors are review thresholds; inspect duration and user impact before acting.

Measurement details:
Shows the highest value among the selected resources at the end of the time window. The resource is named below. Orange starts at 80%, red at 90%; these are initial reference colors, not proof of an outage. See the historical charts for duration and trend. Five-minute CPU utilization averaged across the server logical processors. Namespace does not filter servers.
display.name: Busiest server: CPU used

display.description:
Highest filesystem-use percentage among measured hosts and mounts. The label identifies the filesystem to investigate.

Measurement details:
Shows the highest value among the selected resources at the end of the time window. The resource is named below. Orange starts at 80%, red at 90%; these are initial reference colors, not proof of an outage. See the historical charts for duration and trend. Used space divided by used plus space available to applications, matching df. The mount and device identify the filesystem. Namespace does not filter host disks. Loop devices are excluded: OS images such as Harvester active.img do not represent growing application data. Each device appears once per server; bind mounts of the same filesystem are not counted as separate disks. Use findmnt -S DEVICE on the server to locate its mounts. Operational view: excludes boot, OEM, runtime mounts and kubelet volume mounts. The Harvester persistent partition and all Harvester data disks remain included. Duplicate bind mounts count once per device. Raw collection and space monitors still cover other writable filesystems.
display.name: Fullest host filesystem

display.description:
Average response time per completed host disk operation. Idle disks have no meaningful response-time average.

Measurement details:
Read plus write time divided by completed operations. No value for idle devices. Namespace filters do not apply to server disks.
display.name: Time to read or write a host disk (ms)

display.description:
Difference between committed and applied proposals. A growing gap suggests the database is struggling to apply changes.

Measurement details:
Committed proposals minus applied proposals, per member. Sustained growth means the stored state is falling behind agreed changes.
display.name: Agreed database writes not yet applied

display.description:
99th-percentile etcd backend commit time. Compare with disk latency and pending operations.

Measurement details:
99% of database commits completed within this time. Above 25 ms for five minutes is an initial investigation threshold.
display.name: Database commit time: slowest 1% (ms)

display.description:
Percentage of etcd's configured storage quota used. Review compaction and maintenance procedures before the quota is exhausted.

Measurement details:
Physical database size divided by its quota. Near 100% risks blocking new writes. The initial monitor warns above 80% for ten minutes.
display.name: Database size compared with its quota

display.description:
Estimated failed proposals recorded by each etcd member. Correlate with API errors, leader changes and storage latency.

Measurement details:
Proposals that did not complete through consensus. Compare with elections, connectivity, and logs.
display.name: Failed database operations in 15 minutes

display.description:
Each etcd member should report 1 when it sees a leader. A single healthy member does not provide redundancy.

Measurement details:
Each etcd member should observe a leader. A healthy single-node cluster has no redundancy. Empty results require checking whether etcd collection was enabled and the local endpoint exists.
display.name: Can database members see a leader?

display.description:
Leader changes observed by each database member. Repeated changes may indicate instability; do not sum members as distinct elections.

Measurement details:
Do not add the same election observed by multiple members. Repeated elections can indicate instability; restarts also affect the history.
display.name: Database leader changes in the last hour

display.description:
99th-percentile network round-trip time between etcd members. A single-member cluster may have no peer measurements.

Measurement details:
Time to contact another member and receive a response. A single-member cluster has no peers, so this chart does not apply. Too few observations can also leave it empty.
display.name: Time for database members to communicate (ms)

display.description:
Proposals waiting for consensus in etcd. A sustained queue can explain slow cluster API operations.

Measurement details:
Proposals waiting for consensus. A growing queue can indicate slow disks, network problems, or difficulty reaching a majority of members.
display.name: Database writes waiting for agreement

display.description:
1 means an etcd endpoint was collected successfully. Empty data is expected when optional etcd collection is disabled.

Measurement details:
Shows whether each metrics endpoint answered the collector. This does not prove healthy consensus. Also check leadership and expected member count.
display.name: Can we collect cluster database metrics?

display.description:
99th-percentile time to flush the etcd write-ahead log, in milliseconds. Slow storage can affect the whole cluster control plane.

Measurement details:
99% of write-ahead log flushes completed within this time. Above 10 ms for five minutes is an initial investigation threshold.
display.name: Database log write time: slowest 1% (ms)

display.description:
Percentage used on monitored host filesystems. Review the device and mount point; not every exposed device is a separate physical disk.

Measurement details:
Used space divided by used plus space available to applications. Reserved blocks are excluded from this denominator. Each mount is identified. Loop devices are excluded: OS images such as Harvester active.img do not represent growing application data. Each device appears once per server; bind mounts of the same filesystem are not counted as separate disks. Use findmnt -S DEVICE on the server to locate its mounts. Operational view: excludes boot, OEM, runtime mounts and kubelet volume mounts. The Harvester persistent partition and all Harvester data disks remain included. Duplicate bind mounts count once per device. Raw collection and space monitors still cover other writable filesystems.
display.name: Host filesystem space used

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join((((max by (cluster_name,node,device,fstype) (node_filesystem_size_bytes{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",job="sre-node",device!~"/dev/loop[0-9]+",fstype!~"tmpfs|overlay|squashfs",mountpoint!~"/var/lib/kubelet/.*|/var/lib/rancher/(rke2|k3s)/agent/kubelet/.*|/boot(/.*)?|/run(/.*)?|/oem"})) - (max by (cluster_name,node,device,fstype) (node_filesystem_free_bytes{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",job="sre-node",device!~"/dev/loop[0-9]+",fstype!~"tmpfs|overlay|squashfs",mountpoint!~"/var/lib/kubelet/.*|/var/lib/rancher/(rke2|k3s)/agent/kubelet/.*|/boot(/.*)?|/run(/.*)?|/oem"}))) / clamp_min(((max by (cluster_name,node,device,fstype) (node_filesystem_size_bytes{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",job="sre-node",device!~"/dev/loop[0-9]+",fstype!~"tmpfs|overlay|squashfs",mountpoint!~"/var/lib/kubelet/.*|/var/lib/rancher/(rke2|k3s)/agent/kubelet/.*|/boot(/.*)?|/run(/.*)?|/oem"})) - (max by (cluster_name,node,device,fstype) (node_filesystem_free_bytes{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",job="sre-node",device!~"/dev/loop[0-9]+",fstype!~"tmpfs|overlay|squashfs",mountpoint!~"/var/lib/kubelet/.*|/var/lib/rancher/(rke2|k3s)/agent/kubelet/.*|/boot(/.*)?|/run(/.*)?|/oem"}))) + (max by (cluster_name,node,device,fstype) (node_filesystem_avail_bytes{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",job="sre-node",device!~"/dev/loop[0-9]+",fstype!~"tmpfs|overlay|squashfs",mountpoint!~"/var/lib/kubelet/.*|/var/lib/rancher/(rke2|k3s)/agent/kubelet/.*|/boot(/.*)?|/run(/.*)?|/oem"})), 1)), "sre_series", " · ", "cluster_name", "node", "device"))

display.description: Are servers and applications available, and is the cluster running out of resources?
display.name: What this dashboard tells you

spec.text: **Are servers and applications available, and is the cluster running out of resources?** Start with server readiness and unavailable application replicas. A replica is one instance of an application: if 3 are configured and only 2 are available, 1 is unavailable. Use the application list below to find the affected workload. Brief gaps can occur during updates. **No data is not the same as zero.** Use the description icon for measurement details.

display.description:
Percentage of server CPU time spent busy. Includes applications and platform processes.

Measurement details:
Average utilization across logical processors. Compare sustained high values with CPU limits and slow applications.
display.name: CPU used on each server

display.description:
Percentage of RAM the operating system considers available, including reclaimable cache. Lower means less headroom.

Measurement details:
Linux MemAvailable divided by MemTotal. Lower values mean less headroom. Kubernetes requests are not used in this calculation.
display.name: Memory available on each server

display.description:
Percentage of inode entries used. A filesystem can run out of file entries even when bytes remain available.

Measurement details:
Inodes represent files. They can run out even when bytes remain free. This percentage is calculated only when the inode total is positive. Loop devices are excluded: OS images such as Harvester active.img do not represent growing application data. Each device appears once per server; bind mounts of the same filesystem are not counted as separate disks. Use findmnt -S DEVICE on the server to locate its mounts. Operational view: excludes boot, OEM, runtime mounts and kubelet volume mounts. The Harvester persistent partition and all Harvester data disks remain included. Duplicate bind mounts count once per device. Raw collection and space monitors still cover other writable filesystems.
display.name: Filesystem file entries used

display.description:
Average disk operations in progress over the measurement window. Compare with disk response time to interpret a sustained queue.

Measurement details:
Average outstanding I/O at the Linux block layer, including queued and in-service operations. A sustained rise with disk latency suggests contention. On a Kubernetes VM this is its guest block device; on Harvester this is the host device. Do not sum partitions and their parent disks.
display.name: Disk operations waiting or in progress (operations)

display.description:
Highest server memory-use percentage after allowing for reclaimable memory. Review available RAM and workload growth.

Measurement details:
Shows the highest value among the selected resources at the end of the time window. The resource is named below. Orange starts at 80%, red at 90%; these are initial reference colors, not proof of an outage. See the historical charts for duration and trend. Linux total minus available memory, divided by total. Reclaimable cache is accounted for in available memory. Namespace does not filter servers.
display.name: Busiest server: memory used

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join((last_over_time((topk(1, (1 - (max by (cluster_name,node) (last_over_time(node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",job="sre-node"}[5m])) / max by (cluster_name,node) (last_over_time(node_memory_MemTotal_bytes{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",job="sre-node"}[5m]))))))[1s:1s] @ end())), "sre_series", " · ", "cluster_name", "node"))

display.description:
Major page faults per second on each host. Compare with available memory and application latency.

Measurement details:
Major page faults require disk I/O; file-backed pages also count. Compare this with available RAM and VM swap charts before concluding memory shortage. Linux PSI panels are omitted because these kernels do not expose PSI.
display.name: Host memory pages fetched from disk (pages/s)

display.description:
Total number of configured application instances that are not available. For example, 3 configured and 2 available means 1 unavailable replica. This counts instances, not applications or lost data. Check the named applications below; brief gaps during updates can be normal.

Measurement details:
Only workloads with fewer available copies than configured are listed. The value is the number missing, not a count of failures. Deployment, StatefulSet and DaemonSet names identify the owner. A brief rollout can create a temporary gap. No matching source data stays empty.
display.name: Unavailable application replicas

spec.query: sum(label_replace((label_replace((max by (cluster_name,namespace,deployment) (kubernetes_state_deployment_replicas_unavailable{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",namespace=~"${platform_namespace}"})), "workload", "$1", "deployment", "(.*)")), "kind", "Deployment", "", "") or label_replace((label_replace((max by (cluster_name,namespace,daemonset) (kubernetes_state_daemonset_daemons_unavailable{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",namespace=~"${platform_namespace}"})), "workload", "$1", "daemonset", "(.*)")), "kind", "DaemonSet", "", "") or label_replace(label_replace((clamp_min(max by (cluster_name,namespace,statefulset) (kubernetes_state_statefulset_replicas_desired{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",namespace=~"${platform_namespace}"}) - max by (cluster_name,namespace,statefulset) (kubernetes_state_statefulset_replicas_ready{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",namespace=~"${platform_namespace}"}),0)), "workload", "$1", "statefulset", "(.*)"), "kind", "StatefulSet", "", ""))

display.description:
Receive and transmit errors per second by interface. Sustained increases need a network and host review.

Measurement details:
Receive plus transmit errors. Interface names help distinguish physical and virtual networks.
display.name: Network interface errors (errors/s)

display.description:
Total measured filesystem capacity. Device filters exclude several duplicate or irrelevant mounts.

Measurement details:
Formatted size of the identified mount. It can differ from raw device capacity or the size requested by a PVC. Loop devices are excluded: OS images such as Harvester active.img do not represent growing application data. Each device appears once per server; bind mounts of the same filesystem are not counted as separate disks. Use findmnt -S DEVICE on the server to locate its mounts. Operational view: excludes boot, OEM, runtime mounts and kubelet volume mounts. The Harvester persistent partition and all Harvester data disks remain included. Duplicate bind mounts count once per device. Raw collection and space monitors still cover other writable filesystems.
display.name: Size of host filesystems

display.description:
Bytes used on each monitored server filesystem. Compare the same filesystem with capacity and percentage used.

Measurement details:
Filesystem capacity minus free space. Includes the Harvester data disk and distinguishes partitions. Do not add repeated mounts of one device. Loop devices are excluded: OS images such as Harvester active.img do not represent growing application data. Each device appears once per server; bind mounts of the same filesystem are not counted as separate disks. Use findmnt -S DEVICE on the server to locate its mounts. Operational view: excludes boot, OEM, runtime mounts and kubelet volume mounts. The Harvester persistent partition and all Harvester data disks remain included. Duplicate bind mounts count once per device. Raw collection and space monitors still cover other writable filesystems.
display.name: Space used on host filesystems

display.description:
Count of pods in concerning states, excluding completed jobs. Use the detail list to see whether the issue is scheduling, startup or readiness.

Measurement details:
Counts each Pod once when Pending, Failed, Unknown, or Running but not ready. Completed Jobs are excluded. The list beside this card identifies each Pod. A newly starting Pod may appear briefly; this is a triage list, not an incident declaration.
display.name: Pods needing attention

spec.query: count(max by (cluster_name,namespace,pod_name) (label_replace((max by (cluster_name,namespace,pod_name,pod_phase) (last_over_time(kubernetes_state_pod_status_phase{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",namespace=~"${platform_namespace}",pod_phase!~"Running|Succeeded"}[5m] @ end()) == 1)), "reason", "$1", "pod_phase", "(.*)") or label_replace(((max by (cluster_name,namespace,pod_name) (last_over_time(kubernetes_state_pod_ready{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",namespace=~"${platform_namespace}",condition="false",pod_phase="Running"}[5m] @ end())) == 1)), "reason", "Running but not ready", "", ""))) or (0 * count(kubernetes_state_pod_status_phase{cluster_name=~"${platform_cluster}",namespace=~"${platform_namespace}"}))

display.description:
Names and observed states of affected pods. Read the legend or open details; lines mark inventory entries, not a performance trend.

Measurement details:
Read the table below the line: cluster, namespace, Pod and observed state. Pending may mean scheduling or image preparation; Failed needs Job/container logs; Running but not ready may mean a failed readiness check. Data can lag by a scrape; completed Jobs are excluded.
display.name: Which pods need attention?

display.description:
Current Kubernetes PV status listed by volume. Released requires an ownership and retention review; it is not permission to delete data.

Measurement details:
Bound means attached to a claim; Available means available for a claim; Released requires checking retention policy and data ownership. Released is not always a failure.
display.name: Storage volumes by status

display.description:
Reported filesystem capacity for measured PVCs. This is not the total physical capacity of the storage system.

Measurement details:
Formatted capacity reported by the kubelet. Filesystem metadata can make it smaller than the requested PVC size.
display.name: Size of measured application volumes

display.description:
Current PVC status listed by claim. Pending means the requested storage is not yet bound; inspect provisioning and scheduling events.

Measurement details:
Namespace, claim name, phase, and storage class. Investigate claims that remain Pending.
display.name: Application storage requests by status

display.description:
Percentage used in PVC filesystems that expose usage metrics. Raw block volumes and some drivers cannot supply this measurement.

Measurement details:
Only PVCs with positive inode statistics are included. Block and unmounted volumes are not treated as full.
display.name: Application volume space used

display.description:
Claims lacking filesystem usage measurements. This can be expected for block volumes; verify the storage mode before treating it as a fault.

Measurement details:
Collection inventory, including Block volumes and volumes without mounted-filesystem statistics. Missing data is not a usage percentage.
display.name: Volumes without filesystem usage data

display.description:
Percentage of known nodes reporting Ready. A missing or unready server needs investigation before capacity planning.

Measurement details:
Share of known nodes with the Ready condition. This does not prove that every metrics collector is working.
display.name: Servers ready to run workloads

display.description:
Estimated restart count across selected pods. Rounded to whole restarts for display; counter sampling can affect estimates.

Measurement details:
Sums container restarts within each Pod during a moving hour. The table identifies Pod and namespace. A restart does not prove OOM: inspect Last State, previous logs, readiness/liveness probes and events. Counter resets and scrape intervals affect the estimate.
display.name: Container restarts in the last hour

display.description:
Estimated container restarts grouped by pod. Inspect previous logs and termination reasons; a restart alone does not prove a memory problem.

Measurement details:
Sums container restarts within each Pod during a moving hour. The table identifies Pod and namespace. A restart does not prove OOM: inspect Last State, previous logs, readiness/liveness probes and events. Counter resets and scrape intervals affect the estimate.
display.name: Which pods restarted in the last hour?
